host_story: Mariana traded a Mexico City kitchen job for a jungle villa and never looked back. She cooks plant-forward dinners that even the surfers plan their day around.
name: Sayulita Jungle Yoga Villa
story: A private villa folded into the jungle a short walk above Sayulita's beach break. Two yoga sessions a day, seven guests maximum, and dinners under string lights that end whenever the conversation does.

host_story: Valeria ran wellness programs at a big Costa Rica resort until she decided small was better. Her casa keeps to eight guests and a strict no-rush policy.
name: Santa Teresa Slow Surf Casa
story: A beach-road casa where the day is built around two tides and one long lunch. Boards and bikes included, cold brew on tap, and howler monkeys as your only alarm clock.

host_story: Elena came to Fuerteventura for one windy season fifteen years ago and stayed. She runs the finca with her sister and a rescue dog named Levante.
name: Fuerteventura Wind and Waves Finca
story: A volcanic-stone finca ten minutes from Flag Beach, with wind gear in the barn and boards in the hallway. Kite when it blows, surf when it does not, and stargaze from the courtyard either way.

host_story: Cole grew up in Vancouver, learned to surf on weekend runs to the island, and finally moved out to the coast for good. He splits wood for the sauna himself.
name: Tofino Cedar Surf Lodge
story: A cedar lodge in the rainforest five minutes from Cox Bay, built for cold-water surf and storm watching. Thick wetsuits in every size, a wood-fired sauna for after, and whales passing the headland in spring.

host_story: Joao grew up bodyboarding Ribeira d'Ilhas before it was a world reserve. He opened the lodge so traveling surfers could feel like locals by day two.
name: Ericeira Cliffside Surf Lodge
story: A clifftop lodge in Europe's first World Surfing Reserve, with six named breaks inside a ten minute drive. Communal dinners on Thursdays, board demos from the shaper next door, and sunsets that stop the kitchen.

host_story: Putu built the retreat with bamboo from his uncle's grove and a carpenter cousin. He greets every guest with fresh coconut and the day's swell report.
name: Uluwatu Bamboo Retreat
story: Open-air bamboo bungalows on the cliff above the cave at Uluwatu. Morning flow facing the Indian Ocean, scooter runs to Padang Padang when it fires, and warungs a barefoot walk away.

host_story: Ahmed skippered dive boats for a decade before refitting his own dhoni for surf charters. He knows which atoll pass works on every tide and swell angle.
name: Maldives Atoll Surf Charter
story: Seven nights living on the water, chasing empty reef passes between atolls. Wake at anchor beside the wave, surf until your arms give out, and eat grilled fish while the captain plans tomorrow's crossing.

host_story: Sofia grew up between her family's horses and the Alentejo coast. She pairs every retreat week with rides through the pines to empty Atlantic beaches.
name: Alentejo Horse and Yoga Farmstay
story: A rice-country farmstay where mornings start in the yoga barn and end on horseback in the dunes. Long lunches under the cork oaks, white sand twenty minutes away, and phones that stop mattering by day two.

host_story: Ingrid surfed her first arctic wave at Unstad in a snowstorm and calls it the best decision of her life. She bakes cinnamon buns for every post-surf sauna.
name: Lofoten Arctic Surf Cabin
story: Surf inside the Arctic Circle with snow on the peaks and nobody out. Wood-fired sauna on the beach, northern lights on clear nights, and cabins built for storms and long breakfasts.

host_story: Miguel started as a boatman ferrying surfers to Cloud 9 and saved for six years to open the hostel. He still calls the tide window for guests every morning.
name: Siargao Island Surf Hostel
story: A palm-shaded hostel five minutes from the Cloud 9 boardwalk, built around one long communal table. Island hopping on flat days, reef trips at dawn, and the cheapest good coffee in General Luna.

host_story: Marlon grew up fishing this stretch of coast with his father and knows every sandbar by name. He built the ranch cabins with timber milled an hour inland.
name: Popoyo Offshore Surf Ranch
story: Offshore wind nearly all year and a reef that handles every swell. Cabins face the break, horses graze between them, and the nearest traffic light is two hours away.

host_story: Ishara taught herself to surf on a borrowed board between shifts at her family's guesthouse. Now she runs the house and the morning lineup briefing.
name: Ahangama Palm Surf House
story: A palm-garden house on the south coast's mellowest stretch, with reef and beach breaks in walking distance. Rice and curry lunches, slow train rides to Ella on flat days, and hammocks that claim your afternoon.

host_story: Eleni left an Athens architecture studio to restore her grandmother's house above the bay. She still sketches every sunset from the terrace.
name: Paros Cycladic Yoga House
story: A restored Cycladic house of white walls and blue shutters over a quiet bay. Sunrise yoga on the roof, long swims before lunch, and tavernas that treat you like family by the second night.
